disagreements.sentence_text:
In multivariable analyses within the T2DM cohort, serum testosterone was not independently associated with the ASCVD risk score or any individual cardiometabolic risk factor.

Conclusion

Men with T2DM have a higher estimated 10-year ASCVD risk than non-diabetic controls, irrespective of testosterone status, with T2DM men with low testosterone showing a more adverse cardiometabolic profile.

Transitioning from a metabolically healthy to a metabolically unhealthy phenotype (OR 1.66 [1.19, 2.30]), transitioning from a metabolically unhealthy to a metabolically healthy phenotype (OR 1.56 [1.08, 2.24]), and maintaining a stable metabolically unhealthy status (OR 1.88 [1.39, 2.54]) were significantly associated with an increased risk of incident CVD, CKD and T2DM composite; disease-specific analyses indicated that this association was driven primarily by T2DM.

Conclusions

Our analyses revealed that anthropometric measures, metabolic phenotypes, and dietary patterns are associated with CVD, CKD, and T2DM among individuals with overweight and obesity, especially T2DM.
